assumptions: The codes never occur as real values
avoid_when: Every number is a real measurement
data_needs: Columns with placeholder codes
about.example: A temperature of -99 becomes a missing value.
outputs: The same columns with the codes turned into gaps

about.title: Placeholder numbers to missing

above.description: Values strictly above this are missing

assumptions: Spend and sales can be summed; prices and rates are averaged (choose per column)
Incomplete first and last periods are dropped when full periods are required
avoid_when: Your data already has one row per week or month
The numbers cannot be added up and averaging would hide what matters
data_needs: A date column with a regular rhythm
about.example: Daily TV spend of 100 every day becomes 700 for the week ending Sunday.
about.expert_notes: Group-by on the time coordinate at the target frequency (pandas offset alias); `how` per variable (sum, mean, last); `full_periods_only` drops partial bins.
outputs: The same columns with one row per week or month
about.summary_plain: Adds up daily (or hourly) numbers into one number per week or month, so every row covers the same length of time.
about.title: Weekly or monthly totals
use_when: Your data is daily but you plan and report by week or month
A model expects weekly data

full_periods_only.description: Drop periods that are not fully covered by the source data
full_periods_only.title: Full Periods Only

skipna.description: Ignore missing values (a period with only missing values stays NaN)
skipna.title: Skipna

steps.summary: Aggregate a time dim to a coarser frequency
steps.summary_plain: Turns daily data into weekly or monthly totals

assumptions: The shape and its settings are fixed by you, not learned from the data
avoid_when: The model learns saturation itself (the Bayesian MMM does)
data_needs: Media spend or exposure
about.example: With half-saturation at 1000, spending 1000 gives half the possible effect.
about.expert_notes: Logistic (lam), Hill (slope, half) or Michaelis-Menten curves applied element-wise.
outputs: Media columns on a curved scale
about.summary_plain: Bends spend so that each extra unit of money adds a little less than the one before, as happens when a channel gets saturated.
about.title: Diminishing returns
use_when: You model media with a simple model and need diminishing returns

by.description: Dim whose levels key per-level parameters
by.title: By

steps.summary: Saturation curve with fixed parameters
steps.summary_plain: Models diminishing returns of extra spend

assumptions: Empty combinations can be dropped and are remembered so they can be restored
avoid_when: The model can use the grid directly
data_needs: Two or more dimensions to combine
about.example: 3 markets by 4 products become 12 market-product cells.
outputs: One combined dimension
about.summary_plain: Combines several dimensions, such as market and product, into one list of cells.
about.title: Combine dimensions
use_when: A model works on a flat list of cells instead of a grid

steps.summary: Stack dims into one
steps.summary_plain: Combines several dimensions into a single list of cells

assumptions: Average and spread are learned on the training data only
avoid_when: Zero must keep its meaning (spend of zero should stay zero)
data_needs: Numeric columns
about.example: Temperatures averaging 15 with spread 5 make 20 degrees become 1.0.
outputs: The same columns with average 0 and spread 1
about.summary_plain: Shifts each series so its average is zero and stretches it so its typical spread is one.
about.title: Centre and scale
use_when: You compare the size of effects across inputs measured in different units

fill_mean.description: Mean used for unseen levels with 'fill'

fill_sd.description: SD used for unseen levels with 'fill'
fill_sd.title: Fill Sd

steps.summary: Standardise to zero mean and unit variance over the named dims
steps.summary_plain: Centres each series and scales it to unit spread

assumptions: Padding cells are marked as missing or by a mask
avoid_when: Every group has the same number of rows and the model expects a grid
data_needs: A group dimension (customer) and a position dimension (trip number)
about.example: Household 1 with 3 trips and household 2 with 1 trip becomes 4 rows.
outputs: The same values with one row per observation and a group index
about.summary_plain: Rearranges a table where each group's rows sit side by side into one row per observation, dropping the empty padding.
about.title: One row per observation
use_when: A model works on individual observations, such as shopping trips
Groups have very different numbers of rows

drop_missing.description: Drop rows where every listed variable is missing
drop_missing.title: Drop Missing

mask.description: Boolean padding mask (one of vars); rows where it is False go
mask.title: Mask

vars.description: Every variable on the padded grid

steps.summary: Padded ragged data to long form

assumptions: Gaps are marked so the model can skip them
avoid_when: Your data is already a grid
data_needs: A group column and an order within each group
about.example: Households with 3 and 1 trips become a 2 by 3 grid with two empty cells.
outputs: A grid of groups by position plus a mask of the real cells
about.summary_plain: Lines up each group's rows side by side in a grid, filling short groups with gaps that are marked as missing.
about.title: Line groups up side by side
use_when: A model expects a grid of groups by position, such as households by trip

assumptions: The drift continues at the same rate into the future
avoid_when: The trend changes direction often (use a flexible trend model)
data_needs: A regular date column
about.example: Week 1 gets 0, week 52 gets 1, and week 104 gets 2.
outputs: A trend column (optionally curved)
about.summary_plain: Adds a column that counts up over time, so a model can capture a steady rise or fall.
about.title: Steady drift over time

assumptions: The parts of every combined label are known
